snippet.title: Marcaron en su propia portería A PROPÓSITO para ganar ⚽ #shorts
snippet.description:
Barbados contra Granada, 27 de enero de 1994, clasificación para la Copa del Caribe. Barbados necesitaba ganar por dos goles, y los organizadores habían puesto una regla rara: en la prórroga, el primer gol ganaba el partido y valía doble. Iban 2-0, Granada marcó en el minuto 83 y en el 87 Terry Sealey metió el balón en su propia portería para forzar la prórroga. Desde ese momento Granada podía pasar con cualquier gol, también uno en su propia portería, así que Barbados defendió las dos porterías. En la prórroga, Trevor Thorne marcó el gol de oro: 4-2. El entrenador de Granada, James Clarkson, se quejó de que en el fútbol se marca al rival, no a favor del rival, y la regla no se volvió a usar en la Copa del Caribe.

Las fuentes no coinciden en todo: no está claro quién ideó el autogol ni en qué minuto exacto de la prórroga llegó el gol de oro, por eso no salen en el vídeo. Las imágenes son una recreación, no fotos reales.

Si quieres aprender más, métete en mi perfil.

When asked about the greatest play he’s ever been a part of, the Minnesota Vikings superstar went straight back to November 13, 2022, against the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium. With about two minutes left and Minnesota trailing 27-23, Kirk Cousins told Jefferson there wasn’t much they could call and that he might just have to throw it up and hope JJ came down with it. That’s exactly what happened. On 4th and 18, Cousins launched the ball down the right sideline, and Jefferson climbed the ladder over Bills defensive back Cam Lewis, who already had two hands on the ball, and ripped it away with ONE HAND for a 32-yard gain while falling to the ground. If he doesn’t make that catch, the game is over. Instead, the Vikings stayed alive and went on to beat Josh Allen and the Bills 33-30 in overtime, with Jefferson finishing with 10 catches for a career-high 193 yards and a touchdown in one of the craziest games in NFL history. Ever since, fans and analysts have argued over whether JJ’s grab or Odell Beckham Jr.’s legendary one-handed touchdown against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday Night Football in 2014 is the greatest catch of all time. Pat McAfee brought up the debate, and Shannon Sharpe gave his verdict to Skip Bayless on Undisputed: OBJ’s catch was phenomenal, but it wasn’t 4th and 18 in the fourth quarter in a do-or-die situation! Jefferson’s catch went on to win the ESPY for Best Play, was named the Next Gen Stats Moment of the Year at NFL Honors, and his gloves and arm sleeve were sent to the Pro Football Hall of Fame. Now in the 2026 NFL season, Jefferson is still making highlight-reel grabs for the Vikings, including his jaw-dropping touchdown catch against the Detroit Lions in Week 8. But when you factor in the stakes, the pressure, and the defender with two hands on the ball, does Justin Jefferson’s 4th and 18 catch beat OBJ’s catch as the greatest in NFL history?
